problem: How to use the web to spread knowledge without selling it.
title: MIT decides to publish materials for nearly all its courses free online
context: Universities were debating whether and how to sell online courses.
decision_made: Make materials for nearly all courses freely available online over ten years.
action_taken: Announced by President Charles Vest in April 2001 with an initial goal of over 500 courses; foundations granted $11 million to launch.
observed_outcome: By 2004 about half of MIT's roughly 950 professors were taking part, and MIT paid a $3,000 stipend per course added. Other universities said they would review their own online plans.
lessons: Giving content away can still be sustainable if funded and if faculty are given an incentive to contribute.
limitations: No formal evaluation of learning outcomes or usage was found in the sources used. Early evidence is anecdotal.

claims.claim_text: MIT announced it would make materials for nearly all courses freely available online over ten years.
About half of MIT's professors were participating by 2004.
